headline: Calf test passed (7.2 and 8.0 km, pain-free): resume continuous easy running at ~30 km, no speed, volume capped by the calf gate.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 22 November 2026

Shep — the calf test passed: two clean runs, and running resumes. Hold course; the plan extends a week, with volume still capped by what the calf has shown.

## The week (16–22 Nov)

Done: **25.2 km over three runs** — 10.0 (Tue), 7.2 (Sat), 8.0 (Sun) — plus bike Mon, rest Wed/Thu/Fri. Planned ~38, but Tuesday's 10 km exposed the calf, so the plan correctly swapped runs for bike. All RPE 1, HR 132–139, achilles 0.

- **Tue 17:** felt "like a bruise" the whole way. That ended the test series and the stop was right.
- **Thu 19 physio:** a gastrocnemius strain, treated; her rule is run, stop above 3/10. It replaces my 0/10 gate.
- **Sat 21:** 7.2 km at 5:19, "no pain in the calf". **Sun 22:** 8.0 km at 5:11, "all good". Pace and HR were right, nothing pushed. Sunday was prescribed ~30 min and you ran 8 km (~42 min); fine on this occasion since it was clean, but note it is the same step-over-prescription as 14 Nov, which ended up felt three days later. Hold to the prescribed distances this week.

## Calf and achilles

Two runs is encouraging, not yet proof. The pattern in the 11–17 Nov block was fine, fine, then felt all the way. So Tuesday's run and the following morning matter more than these two. A gastrocnemius strain is loaded by pace and push-off, so keeping everything at 5:15/km or slower with no strides is the real protection, more than distance. Achilles 0 throughout; no prodrome reported. Straight-knee calf work from the physio is what earns speed back later.

## Recovery

HRV 7-day baseline 32 → 33; last night 35 (UNBALANCED, up from the 28–31 range), RHR 47–49, sleep 81–87, 7.9–8.7 h. Slightly improving, still below the 36 it held through October. Load is very low (ACWR 0.5–0.8), so this is not training fatigue, and you've said you feel fine, which under your 15 Nov overrule I'm honouring. One risk sentence: unexplained HRV flatness is also what illness looks like early, so chest symptoms, temperature or aches mean no hard session. Nothing in your notes suggests that.

## Efficiency and base

Easy pace 5:12–5:19 at HR 132–139, efficiency 1.42 for the week against 1.48 last week. That is slower pace at similar HR, which fits holding 5:15+ deliberately and returning from a layoff, not a loss of fitness. VO2 max reads 57, unchanged. Judge the base over weeks, not off this one.

## Load check

`volume_target.json`: 23–29 Nov `held` by the calf gate (curve 67.9, ramp cap 31.5); 30 Nov `over` at the old plan's 27 because it was built off a 12 km base; 7 Dec unplanned. I have not chased the curve — the gate stands, and you are about 40 km a week behind the November shape. I'm saying it plainly: that gap is the calf's, and it is recoverable (the March peak needs under 2 km/week on average only if the climb starts soon). The proposal rebuilds from the actual 25 km base inside the cap:

- **23–29 Nov: 30 km** (Tue 6, Wed 5, Thu 6, Sat 6, Sun 7). Gym legs twice, per physio.
- **30 Nov–6 Dec, provisional: 37 km**, long run 10 returns on the Sunday.
- **7–13 Dec, provisional: 42 km**, long run 12; XC on 13 Dec skipped by default.

If this week is silent, the next review pushes toward the curve through easy volume and the long run. Intensity does not return in the same weeks as volume: no strides until 2–3 weeks symptom-free, none quicker than 3:15/km, and after a proper warm-up when below ~8 °C.

## Admin and countdown

Wokingham Half (21 Feb, the PB attempt, 17 s from 1:20:46) — entry at end-of-November payday; it sells out. Fission 20 opens 1 Jan. Blood re-test 6–12 January, rested, morning. Manchester is 21 weeks out; the layoff costs weeks of volume, not fitness, and sub-3 is intact.

## Recommendation: hold

Resume easy running under the physio's rule, continuous from Tuesday, no strides, distances as prescribed.
